metadata.title: Part One • 10 Steps To Building Your Own Family Tree • Fraser and Fraser
metadata.author: Fraser and Fraser
metadata.shortDescription:
Part one of our top 10 tips to building your own family tree. Whether you're a genealogy buff, fascinated by ancestry or would like to track down long lost family, Fraser & Fraser's advice could help.

Don't forget to view Part Two!

www.fraserandfraser.co.uk

segments.text: thanks to the internet it's never been
easier to trace your family tree
however it's quite a daunting task
setting off and knowing what's correct
where to look
in this series of films we're going to
try and give you a few hints to tell you
how to get started and how to build your
very own family tree
get the biggest piece of paper you can
find and jot down all you know about
your family in the form of the family
tree it's best to look online for a
template and the best thing is to put
yourself in the middle and then work
outwards check down all the information
you know about your parents
your grandparents
your aunts and uncles
your great aunts and uncles
it's surprising how much you'll know
about your own family
my advice would be to start with talking
with your parents even better if your
grandparents were alive
don't lead the questions get them to
answer in their own way we always find
that the best people to talk to and know
the most are the females in the family
see if you can place any of the photos
on the family tree
also look at the back to see if there's
names dates or places of where the photo
was taken this can greatly reduce death
searches later on
do you want to follow online back as far
as you can
research your parents your grandparents
your great grandparents so you end up
with a family tree that's like an upside
down pyramid do you want to research
ancestors going back as far as you can
or even research forward finding
relatives or simply just a one named
study researching one particular survey
the first thing you're going to want to
decide when you're mapping out your
findings is whether you're going to draw
it out on a family tree with pen and
paper the old fashioned the cheaper way
or as we would advise get yourself a
good family history piece of software
and that means that every time you need
to change your family tree you can make
the changes to the software and they'll
change the outline of the tree for you
means you won't be crossing out and
rubbing things out all the time makes
things smoother quicker and easier
don't feel as if you need to go for the
most expensive one on the market have a
look at your options it may be that
there's cheaper ones that will do
everything you needed to do
have a look around see what features you
want and get the best program for you
